sanskrit: svabhāvajena kaunteya nibaddhaḥ svena karmaṇā kartuṃ necchasi yan mohāt kariṣyasy avaśo 'pi tat
english: Bound, O son of Kuntī, by your own deeds born of your innate nature, that very thing which in delusion you wish not to do, you shall do even against your will.

sanskrit: īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛddeśe 'rjuna tiṣṭhati bhrāmayan sarvabhūtāni yantrārūḍhāni māyayā
english: The Lord, O Arjuna, dwells in the heart-region of all beings, whirling all beings round by his māyā as though they were mounted upon a machine.

sanskrit: tam eva śaraṇaṃ gaccha sarvabhāvena bhārata tatprasādāt parāṃ śāntiṃ sthānaṃ prāpsyasi śāśvatam
english: To him alone go for refuge with your whole being, O Bhārata; by his grace you shall attain the supreme peace and the eternal abode.

sanskrit: iti te jñānam ākhyātaṃ guhyād guhyataraṃ mayā vimṛśyaitad aśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru
english: Thus has the knowledge, more secret than all that is secret, been declared to you by me. Ponder it fully, and then act as you will.

sanskrit: sarvaguhyatamaṃ bhūyaḥ śṛṇu me paramaṃ vacaḥ iṣṭo 'si me dṛḍham iti tato vakṣyāmi te hitam
english: Hear again my supreme word, the most secret of all. Because you are dearly beloved by me, I shall now declare to you what is for your good.

sanskrit: manmanā bhava madbhakto madyājī māṃ namaskuru mām evaiṣyasi satyaṃ te pratijāne priyo 'si me
english: Fix your mind on me, be devoted to me, sacrifice to me, bow down to me. To me alone you shall come; truly I promise you this, for you are dear to me.

sanskrit: sarvadharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ
english: Abandoning all duties, come to me alone for refuge. I shall liberate you from all sins; grieve not.

sanskrit: idaṃ te nātapaskāya nābhaktāya kadā cana na cāśuśrūṣave vācyaṃ na ca māṃ yo 'bhyasūyati
english: This is never to be told by you to one who practices no austerity, nor to one without devotion, nor to one who does not wish to listen, nor to one who scoffs at me.

sanskrit: ya idaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ madbhakteṣv abhidhāsyati bhaktiṃ mayi parāṃ kṛtvā mām evaiṣyaty asaṃśayaḥ
english: Whoever shall declare this supreme secret among my devotees, rendering the highest devotion to me, shall come to me alone, without doubt.

sanskrit: na ca tasmān manuṣyeṣu kaś cin me priyakṛttamaḥ bhavitā na ca me tasmād anyaḥ priyataro bhuvi
english: And among men there shall be none who renders me more cherished service than he, nor shall there be another on earth dearer to me than he.

sanskrit: adhyeṣyate ca ya imaṃ dharmyaṃ saṃvādam āvayoḥ jñānayajñena tenāham iṣṭaḥ syām iti me matiḥ
english: And whoever shall study this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: śraddhāvān anasūyaś ca śṛṇuyād api yo naraḥ so 'pi muktaḥ śubhāṃl lokān prāpnuyāt puṇyakarmaṇām
english: And the man who, full of faith and free from spite, should merely listen to it—he too, set free, shall attain the blessed worlds of those whose deeds are meritorious.

sanskrit: kaccid etac chrutaṃ pārtha tvayaikāgreṇa cetasā kaccid ajñānasaṃmohaḥ pranaṣṭas te dhanaṃjaya
english: Has this been heard by you, O Pārtha, with a mind fixed upon one point? Has the delusion born of ignorance been destroyed in you, O Dhanaṃjaya?

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca naṣṭo mohaḥ smṛtir labdhā tvatprasādān mayācyuta sthito 'smi gatasaṃdehaḥ kariṣye vacanaṃ tava
english: Arjuna said: My delusion is destroyed, and through your grace, O Acyuta, I have regained my memory. I stand firm, my doubts dispelled; I will do your word.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity ahaṃ vāsudevasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ saṃvādam imam aśrauṣam adbhutaṃ romaharṣaṇam
english: Saṃjaya said: Thus did I hear this marvelous dialogue, making the hair stand on end, between Vāsudeva and the great-souled Pārtha.

sanskrit: vyāsaprasādāc chrutavān etad guhyam ahaṃ param yogaṃ yogeśvarāt kṛṣṇāt sākṣāt kathayataḥ svayam
english: By the grace of Vyāsa I have heard this supreme secret, this yoga, from Kṛṣṇa, the lord of yoga, declaring it in person and with his own voice.

sanskrit: rājan saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya saṃvādam imam adbhutam keśavārjunayoḥ puṇyaṃ hṛṣyāmi ca muhur muhuḥ
english: O king, recalling again and again this wondrous and holy dialogue of Keśava and Arjuna, I thrill with joy time after time.

sanskrit: tac ca saṃsmṛtya saṃsmṛtya rūpam atyadbhutaṃ hareḥ vismayo me mahān rājan hṛṣyāmi ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: And recalling again and again that exceedingly marvelous form of Hari, great is my wonder, O king, and I rejoice over and over.

sanskrit: yatra yogeśvaraḥ kṛṣṇo yatra pārtho dhanurdharaḥ tatra śrīr vijayo bhūtir dhruvā nītir matir mama
english: Wherever there is Kṛṣṇa, the lord of yoga, wherever there is Pārtha the bowman, there are fortune, victory, prosperity, and steadfast righteousness: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato dhanaṃjayaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇagāṇḍīvadhāriṇam punar eva mahānādaṃ vyasṛjanta mahārathāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Then, beholding Dhanaṃjaya bearing his arrows and the Gāṇḍīva bow, the great chariot-warriors once again let loose a mighty roar.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāḥ somakāś caiva ye caiṣām anuyāyinaḥ dadhmuś ca muditāḥ śaṅkhān vīrāḥ sāgarasaṃbhavān
english: The Pāṇḍavas and the Somakas, and those who followed them, gladdened heroes, blew their conches, born of the sea.

sanskrit: tato bheryaś ca peśyaś ca krakacā goviṣāṇikāḥ sahasaivābhyahanyanta tataḥ śabdo mahān abhūt
english: Then kettledrums and tabors, krakaca-trumpets and cow-horns were all struck at once, and a tremendous din arose.

sanskrit: atha devāḥ sagandharvāḥ pitaraś ca janeśvara siddhacāraṇasaṃghāś ca samīyus te didṛkṣayā
english: Then the gods together with the gandharvas and the ancestors, O lord of men, and the hosts of siddhas and cāraṇas, gathered there eager to behold the spectacle.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca mahābhāgāḥ puraskṛtya śatakratum samīyus tatra sahitā draṣṭuṃ tad vaiśasaṃ mahat
english: And the highly blessed sages, placing Śatakratu at their head, assembled there together to witness that great slaughter.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro dṛṣṭvā yuddhāya susamudyate te sene sāgaraprakhye muhuḥ pracalite nṛpa
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, beholding those two armies, vast as the ocean, roused and arrayed for battle and surging again and again, O king—

sanskrit: vimucya kavacaṃ vīro nikṣipya ca varāyudham avaruhya rathāt tūrṇaṃ padbhyām eva kṛtāñjaliḥ
english: the hero loosed his armor, laid aside his excellent weapon, swiftly descended from his chariot, and on foot, with hands joined in reverence—

sanskrit: pitāmaham abhiprekṣya dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vāgyataḥ prayayau yena prāṅmukho ripuvāhinīm
english: gazing toward his grandsire, Yudhiṣṭhira the king of righteousness, with words restrained, set forth, facing eastward, toward the host of the foe.

sanskrit: taṃ prayāntam abhiprekṣya kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ avatīrya rathāt tūrṇaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito 'nvayāt
english: Beholding him setting forth, Dhanaṃjaya the son of Kuntī swiftly stepped down from his chariot and, together with his brothers, followed him.

sanskrit: vāsudevaś ca bhagavān pṛṣṭhato 'nujagāma ha yathāmukhyāś ca rājānas tam anvājagmur utsukāḥ
english: And the lord Vāsudeva walked behind him, and the foremost kings too, full of eagerness, went after him.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca kiṃ te vyavasitaṃ rājan yad asmān apahāya vai padbhyām eva prayāto 'si prāṅmukho ripuvāhinīm
english: Arjuna said: What have you resolved, O king, that leaving us behind you set out on foot, facing eastward toward the army of the enemy?

sanskrit: bhīmasena uvāca kva gamiṣyasi rājendra nikṣiptakavacāyudhaḥ daṃśiteṣv arisainyeṣu bhrātṝn utsṛjya pārthiva
english: Bhīmasena said: Where will you go, O king of kings, with armor and weapons cast aside, while the enemy's hosts stand mailed, and forsaking your brothers, O lord of the earth?

sanskrit: nakula uvāca evaṃgate tvayi jyeṣṭhe mama bhrātari bhārata bhīr me dunoti hṛdayaṃ brūhi gantā bhavān kva nu
english: Nakula said: When you, my eldest brother, go forth in this manner, O Bhārata, fear torments my heart. Tell me, whither do you mean to go?

sanskrit: sahadeva uvāca asmin raṇasamūhe vai vartamāne mahābhaye yoddhavye kva nu gantāsi śatrūn abhimukho nṛpa
english: Sahadeva said: While this dreadful press of battle is upon us and the fight is to be joined, where will you go, advancing thus toward the foe, O king?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca evam ābhāṣyamāṇo 'pi bhrātṛbhiḥ kurunandana novāca vāgyataḥ kiṃ cid gacchaty eva yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Though thus addressed by his brothers, O delight of the Kurus, Yudhiṣṭhira, his speech restrained, said nothing at all, but went straight on.

sanskrit: tān uvāca mahāprājño vāsudevo mahāmanāḥ abhiprāyo 'sya vijñāto mayeti prahasann iva
english: To them the greatly wise and high-minded Vāsudeva spoke, as though smiling: His purpose I have understood.

sanskrit: eṣa bhīṣmaṃ tathā droṇaṃ gautamaṃ śalyam eva ca anumānya gurūn sarvān yotsyate pārthivo 'ribhiḥ
english: This king, having sought the leave of Bhīṣma and Droṇa, of Gautama and of Śalya, indeed of all his elders, will then do battle with his foes.

sanskrit: śrūyate hi purākalpe gurūn ananumānya yaḥ yudhyate sa bhaved vyaktam apadhyāto mahattaraiḥ
english: For it is heard that in the ancient ordinance whoever does battle without seeking the leave of his elders is plainly held in ill regard by those who are greater than he.

sanskrit: anumānya yathāśāstraṃ yas tu yudhyen mahattaraiḥ dhruvas tasya jayo yuddhe bhaved iti matir mama
english: But he who, having sought their leave according to the scriptures, fights with those greater than himself—his is certain victory in war: such is my conviction.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kṛṣṇe tu dhārtarāṣṭracamūṃ prati hāhākāro mahān āsīn niḥśabdās tv apare 'bhavan
english: As Kṛṣṇa spoke thus, in the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son there arose a great cry of dismay, while others among them fell silent.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dūrād dhārtarāṣṭrasya sainikāḥ mithaḥ saṃkathayāṃ cakrur neśo 'sti kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: Seeing Yudhiṣṭhira from afar, the soldiers of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son spoke to one another: This man is a disgrace to his line, undone.

sanskrit: vyaktaṃ bhīta ivābhyeti rājāsau bhīṣmam antikāt yudhiṣṭhiraḥ sasodaryaḥ śaraṇārthaṃ prayācakaḥ
english: Plainly, as if afraid, this king Yudhiṣṭhira approaches Bhīṣma, drawing near with his brothers, a suppliant begging for refuge.

sanskrit: dhanaṃjaye kathaṃ nāthe pāṇḍave ca vṛkodare nakule sahadeve ca bhīto 'bhyeti ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: With Dhanaṃjaya for protector, and Vṛkodara the Pāṇḍava, and Nakula and Sahadeva—how is it that the son of Pāṇḍu comes forward in fear?

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ kṣatriyakule jātaḥ saṃprathite bhuvi yathāsya hṛdayaṃ bhītam alpasattvasya saṃyuge
english: Surely he was not born in a kṣatriya line renowned upon the earth, weak of spirit as he is, whose heart is thus stricken with terror in the fray.

sanskrit: tatas te kṣatriyāḥ sarve praśaṃsanti sma kauravān hṛṣṭāḥ sumanaso bhūtvā cailāni dudhuvuḥ pṛthak
english: Then all those kṣatriyas fell to praising the Kauravas and, become glad and joyful at heart, each waved his garments aloft.

sanskrit: vyanindanta tataḥ sarve yodhās tatra viśāṃ pate yudhiṣṭhiraṃ sasodaryaṃ sahitaṃ keśavena ha
english: Then all the warriors there reviled Yudhiṣṭhira, O lord of the people, together with his brothers and with Keśava.

sanskrit: tatas tat kauravaṃ sainyaṃ dhikkṛtvā tu yudhiṣṭhiram niḥśabdam abhavat tūrṇaṃ punar eva viśāṃ pate
english: Then that Kaurava host, having cried shame upon Yudhiṣṭhira, fell silent again all at once, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu vakṣyati rājāsau kiṃ bhīṣmaḥ prativakṣyati kiṃ bhīmaḥ samaraślāghī kiṃ nu kṛṣṇārjunāv iti
english: What will this king say? What will Bhīṣma answer? What will Bhīma, who glories in battle, say? And what will Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna say?—thus they wondered.

sanskrit: vivakṣitaṃ kim asyeti saṃśayaḥ sumahān abhūt ubhayoḥ senayo rājan yudhiṣṭhirakṛte tadā
english: What does he intend to say? A very great uncertainty then arose in both armies, O king, on account of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sa vigāhya camūṃ śatroḥ śaraśaktisamākulām bhīṣmam evābhyayāt tūrṇaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: Plunging into the enemy's host, thronged with arrows and spears, he swiftly approached Bhīṣma, encircled by his brothers.

sanskrit: tam uvāca tataḥ pādau karābhyāṃ pīḍya pāṇḍavaḥ bhīṣmaṃ śāṃtanavaṃ rājā yuddhāya samupasthitam
english: Then, clasping his feet with both hands, the Pāṇḍava king addressed Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, who stood ready for battle.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āmantraye tvāṃ durdharṣa yotsye tāta tvayā saha anujānīhi māṃ tāta āśiṣaś ca prayojaya
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I take my leave of you, O unassailable one; I shall fight against you, dear father. Grant me your leave, dear father, and bestow upon me your blessings.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca yady evaṃ nābhigacchethā yudhi māṃ pṛthivīpate śapeyaṃ tvāṃ mahārāja parābhāvāya bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: Had you not come to me thus before the battle, O lord of the earth, I should have cursed you, great king, unto your defeat, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: prīto 'smi putra yudhyasva jayam āpnuhi pāṇḍava yat te 'bhilaṣitaṃ cānyat tad avāpnuhi saṃyuge
english: I am pleased, my son; fight, and win victory, O Pāṇḍava. Whatever else you desire, that too may you obtain in the battle.

sanskrit: vriyatāṃ ca varaḥ pārtha kim asmatto 'bhikāṅkṣasi evaṃ gate mahārāja na tavāsti parājayaḥ
english: And let a boon be chosen, O Pārtha; what do you wish from us? When matters stand thus, O great king, defeat shall not be yours.

sanskrit: arthasya puruṣo dāso dāsas tv artho na kasya cit iti satyaṃ mahārāja baddho 'smy arthena kauravaiḥ
english: A man is the slave of wealth, but wealth is no one's slave: this is the truth, O great king. By their wealth I am bound to the Kauravas.

sanskrit: atas tvāṃ klībavad vākyaṃ bravīmi kurunandana hṛto 'smy arthena kauravya yuddhād anyat kim icchasi
english: Therefore I speak to you, O delight of the Kurus, words as of a eunuch: I have been bought with wealth, O Kaurava. What do you desire other than battle?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca mantrayasva mahāprājña hitaiṣī mama nityaśaḥ yudhyasva kauravasyārthe mamaiṣa satataṃ varaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Counsel me, O greatly wise one, ever seeking my good; fight for the Kaurava's sake. This is forever the boon I ask of you.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca rājan kim atra sāhyaṃ te karomi kurunandana kāmaṃ yotsye parasyārthe brūhi yat te vivakṣitam
english: Bhīṣma said: O king, what help can I render you in this, O delight of the Kurus? Fight I shall, willingly, for another's sake; tell me what you wish to say.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ jayeyaṃ saṃgrāme bhavantam aparājitam etan me mantraya hitaṃ yadi śreyaḥ prapaśyasi
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How may I conquer you, unvanquished, in the fray? Counsel me in this for my good, if you see what is best.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na taṃ paśyāmi kaunteya yo māṃ yudhyantam āhave vijayeta pumān kaś cid api sākṣāc chatakratuḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: I see no man, O son of Kuntī, who could vanquish me as I fight in the battle—not even Śatakratu himself in person.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca hanta pṛcchāmi tasmāt tvāṃ pitāmaha namo 'stu te jayopāyaṃ bravīhi tvam ātmanaḥ samare paraiḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Then, grandsire, I ask you—homage be to you—tell me yourself the means by which you may be overcome by foes in battle.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca na śatruṃ tāta paśyāmi samare yo jayeta mām na tāvan mṛtyukālo me punarāgamanaṃ kuru
english: Bhīṣma said: I see no enemy, my child, who could conquer me in battle; the hour of my death has not yet come. Come to me again.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato yudhiṣṭhiro vākyaṃ bhīṣmasya kurunandana śirasā pratijagrāha bhūyas tam abhivādya ca
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, O delight of the Kurus, received Bhīṣma's words with bowed head and once more saluted him.

sanskrit: prāyāt punar mahābāhur ācāryasya rathaṃ prati paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ madhyena bhrātṛbhiḥ saha
english: Then the mighty-armed one set forth again toward the teacher's chariot, in full view of all the armies, passing through their midst together with his brothers.

sanskrit: sa droṇam abhivādyātha kṛtvā caiva pradakṣiṇam uvāca vācā durdharṣam ātmaniḥśreyasaṃ vacaḥ
english: Having saluted Droṇa and made the rightward circumambulation about him, he spoke to that unassailable one a word that sought his own highest good.

sanskrit: āmantraye tvāṃ bhagavan yotsye vigatakalmaṣaḥ jayeyaṃ ca ripūn sarvān anujñātas tvayā dvija
english: I take my leave of you, O venerable one; I shall fight, freed of all guilt, and may I conquer all my foes when granted your leave, O brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca yadi māṃ nābhigacchethā yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ śapeyaṃ tvāṃ mahārāja parābhāvāya sarvaśaḥ
english: Droṇa said: Had you not come to me, resolved upon battle, I should have cursed you wholly, great king, unto your utter defeat.

sanskrit: tad yudhiṣṭhira tuṣṭo 'smi pūjitaś ca tvayānagha anujānāmi yudhyasva vijayaṃ samavāpnuhi
english: Therefore, Yudhiṣṭhira, I am content, and honored by you, O sinless one. I grant you leave: fight, and win the victory.

sanskrit: karavāṇi ca te kāmaṃ brūhi yat te 'bhikāṅkṣitam evaṃ gate mahārāja yuddhād anyat kim icchasi
english: And I shall fulfill your desire; tell me what you long for. When matters stand thus, O great king, what do you wish other than battle?

sanskrit: arthasya puruṣo dāso dāsas tv artho na kasya cit iti satyaṃ mahārāja baddho 'smy arthena kauravaiḥ
english: A man is the slave of wealth, but wealth is no one's slave: this is the truth, O great king. By their wealth I am bound to the Kauravas.

sanskrit: atas tvāṃ klībavad brūmo yuddhād anyat kim icchasi yotsyāmi kauravasyārthe tavāśāsyo jayo mayā
english: Therefore I speak to you words as of a eunuch: what do you wish other than battle? I shall fight for the Kaurava's sake, yet your victory is to be wished for by me.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca jayam āśāssva me brahman mantrayasva ca maddhitam yudhyasva kauravasyārthe vara eṣa vṛto mayā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Wish me victory, O brāhmaṇa, and counsel me for my good; fight for the Kaurava's sake. This is the boon I have chosen.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca dhruvas te vijayo rājan yasya mantrī haris tava ahaṃ ca tvābhijānāmi raṇe śatrūn vijeṣyasi
english: Droṇa said: Certain is your victory, O king, you whose counselor is Hari. And I assure you: in battle you shall conquer your foes.

sanskrit: yato dharmas tataḥ kṛṣṇo yataḥ kṛṣṇas tato jayaḥ yudhyasva gaccha kaunteya pṛccha māṃ kiṃ bravīmi te
english: Where there is righteousness, there is Kṛṣṇa; where there is Kṛṣṇa, there is victory. Fight, go forth, O son of Kuntī; ask of me—what shall I tell you?

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śṛṇu me yad vivakṣitam kathaṃ jayeyaṃ saṃgrāme bhavantam aparājitam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: I ask you, O best of the twice-born; hear what I wish to say. How may I conquer you, unvanquished, in the fray?

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca na te 'sti vijayas tāvad yāvad yudhyāmy ahaṃ raṇe mamāśu nidhane rājan yatasva saha sodaraiḥ
english: Droṇa said: There is no victory for you so long as I fight in battle. Strive swiftly, O king, together with your brothers, for my slaying.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca hanta tasmān mahābāho vadhopāyaṃ vadātmanaḥ ācārya praṇipatyaiṣa pṛcchāmi tvāṃ namo 'stu te
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Alas! Then tell me, O mighty-armed one, the means of your own destruction. Bowing low, O teacher, I ask you this—homage be to you.

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca na śatruṃ tāta paśyāmi yo māṃ hanyād raṇe sthitam yudhyamānaṃ susaṃrabdhaṃ śaravarṣaughavarṣiṇam
english: Droṇa said: I see no enemy, my child, who could slay me as I stand in battle, fighting in full fury and pouring forth floods and torrents of arrows—

sanskrit: ṛte prāyagataṃ rājan nyastaśastram acetanam hanyān māṃ yudhi yodhānāṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: save when, O king, I have resolved to fast unto death, have laid down my weapons and grown senseless to the world—then among warriors one might slay me in battle. This truth I tell you.

sanskrit: śastraṃ cāhaṃ raṇe jahyāṃ śrutvā sumahad apriyam śraddheyavākyāt puruṣād etat satyaṃ bravīmi te
english: And I shall cast away my weapons in the battle on hearing some most grievous tidings from a man whose word is to be trusted: this truth I tell you.
